title: Supply problems may force Freeport Indonesia to halt Manyar smelter
body: The $3.7 billion Manyar smelter only resumed operations in May after a fire broke out in October last year.

title: Column: Tin breaks higher as Indonesia cracks down on illegal miners

title: Freeport-McMoRan still in talks with Indonesia over Grasberg mine rights
body: PT Freeport Indonesia is 51% owned by Indonesia's government but operated by Freeport.

title: Freeport to divest 12% of mine to Indonesia, CNBC says
body: The divestment is part of an agreement to extend the company’s license to operate the Grasberg mine.

title: Central Omega Resources Reports Record Production and Profit Surge in H1 2025
body: In the first half of 2025, PT Central Omega Resources Tbk achieved a 140% jump in nickel ore production to 1.73 Mt and a 159% increase in sales to 1.83 Mt, while net profit rose 38% to Rp310.3 bn and EBITDA surged 219% to Rp481.4 bn, driven by the full resumption of mining operations under a new 2024 RKAB. The company remains optimistic for the rest of the year, citing stable global nickel prices, but remains cautious of potential U.S. tariff uncertainties, pledging to sustain momentum through operational efficiency, new reserve exploration, and sustainable resource management.

title: Merdeka Battery Sees 78% Rise in Nickel Ore Production in H1 2025 Despite Revenue Drop
body: In the first half of 2025, Merdeka Battery’s nickel ore output surged 78% to 6.9 Mt wmt, driven by 45% growth in limonite and 189% in saprolite, while revenue fell 32% to US$628 M; the company also cut NPI cash cost to US$9,719/ton and sold 9,465 t of MHP through ESG’s HPAL Train A, with ongoing HPAL and slurry‑pipeline projects set to boost downstream capacity. EBITDA stood at US$77 M, down 8% YOY but up 33% in Q2 after HGNM cuts, underscoring resilient margins amid strategic focus on upstream‑to‑downstream integration.

title: Indonesia Secures 64% of Global Nickel Production, Calls for Consistent Regulation to Boost Downstream Industry
body: Indonesia now controls about 64% of worldwide nickel output, with 424 mining firms and 163 processing plants—including 55 active in pyro‑metallurgy and HPAL—according to APNI Secretary‑General Meidy Katrin Lengkey. She urged the government to maintain stable, investor‑friendly regulations to support the growth of downstream sectors such as stainless steel and battery manufacturing.
